resources.string: Some input is not valid. Check the highlighted fields.
Wrong pairing code. Check the six digits on the TV and try again.
The TV did not answer in time. Keep the pairing screen open on the TV and try again.
The pairing code or port has expired. On the TV, choose \"Pair device with pairing code\" again to get a fresh code and port.
This phone is not paired with the TV yet. Pair it first.
The TV no longer trusts this phone. Pair again to continue.
Wireless debugging seems to be off, or the connect port changed. Turn it on and check the port on the TV.
Can\'t reach the TV. Make sure the phone and TV are on the same Wi-Fi (not a guest network).
The connection timed out. Check that the TV is on and Wireless debugging is enabled.
The TV did not accept that command.
This isn\'t supported by your TV or by this phone\'s Android version.
Local network access is required to reach your TV. Allow \"Nearby devices / local network\" for NEXUS in system settings.
Control your Google TV from your phone over local Wi-Fi.
Pair NEXUS with your Haier or other Google TV using Wireless debugging. It takes about two minutes and only needs to be done once.
Press the Settings (gear) button, then open System → About.
Select \"Android TV OS build\" (or \"Build\") 7 times until the TV says you are now a developer.
Go back to System → Developer options and turn on Wireless debugging. Allow it if the TV asks.
Open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. Keep this screen open on the TV.
Open Settings → System → About. On some TVs it is Settings → Device Preferences → About.
Select \"Build\" (or \"Android TV OS build\") 7 times to enable Developer options.
Open Developer options (under System or Device Preferences) and turn on Wireless debugging.
Choose Pair device with pairing code. The TV shows an IP address, a pairing port and a six-digit code.
Type the IP address, pairing port and six-digit code below.
The connect port is the port shown on the main Wireless debugging screen under \"IP address & port\". It is different from the pairing port.
Your phone and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi network. Guest networks often block devices from seeing each other.
Wireless debugging gives this phone developer-level control of the TV. Pair only on your own trusted network, never share the code, and turn Wireless debugging off when you don\'t need it.
Enter a valid IPv4 address, like 192.168.1.20.
Enter the six digits shown on the TV.
The pairing port and connect port are normally different. Check the main Wireless debugging screen for the connect port.
Paired, but could not connect yet. Check the connect port on the TV\'s main Wireless debugging screen, then retry.
No TV selected. Choose one on the TVs tab.
Controls are disabled until the TV is connected.
This sends the power key. Many TVs cannot be turned back on over Wi-Fi, so you may need the TV\'s own remote to switch it on again.
Connect to a TV to see its apps.
First select a text field on the TV (for example a search box), then type here and tap Send.
Supported characters: letters A–Z, digits 0–9, space and . , ! ? - _ @ : / \' \" ( ) & + = # *. Up to 300 characters. Emoji and other scripts are not supported.
This deletes the saved profile and this phone\'s pairing key for this TV. To fully revoke access, also open Developer options → Revoke debugging authorizations on the TV.
Vibrate briefly when you press a remote button.
Play the system click sound (requires touch sounds to be on).
Ask before sending the power key.
Menu names differ between TV brands and software versions. Try these:
Can\'t find \"Build\": look under Settings → System → About, or Settings → Device Preferences → About. Select the entry named \"Build\" or \"Android TV OS build\" 7 times.
Can\'t find Developer options: after enabling it, look under System, Device Preferences, or at the bottom of the main Settings list.
No Wireless debugging option: your TV may run Android TV 10 or older, or the maker disabled it. NEXUS needs Wireless debugging (Android 11 or newer).
Pairing times out: make sure both devices use the same Wi-Fi band and router, not a guest network, and that the router does not isolate clients.
Connect fails after a TV restart: the connect port changes. Open Wireless debugging on the TV and update the port with Edit.

No data leaves this device. NEXUS has no account, no cloud server, no analytics, no crash reporting and no ads. It talks only to your TV on your local network. TV names, addresses and settings are stored on this phone; the pairing key is encrypted with the Android Keystore. Pairing codes are never stored. Forgetting a TV deletes its profile and key.
Tap a TV below to connect.
Make sure your phone and TV are on the same Wi-Fi network and that Wireless debugging is turned on on the TV.
How to turn on Wireless debugging
Ready to pair · tap to enter the code
Saved · not seen on the network
NEXUS needs permission to find TVs on your Wi-Fi and talk to them. Nothing leaves your network.
Enter the six-digit code shown on your TV.
Open the pairing screen on your TV
On the TV, go to Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. This screen updates by itself when the TV is ready.
This TV is no longer visible on the network. Check that it is on and connected to the same Wi-Fi.
Paired. Waiting for the TV to appear on the network…
Couldn\'t open this app on your TV.
Choose which apps appear on the Remote screen, and their order.
Use the D-pad on your remote to change these settings on the TV.
This setting isn\'t available on your TV.
Connect to a TV to open its settings.
